findings.title: Team admins are rejected by the permission check
findings.description: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. `isTeamAdmin` returns a membership object for ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284), and `isTeamOwner` is true only for OWNER (lines 286-295). The `&&` therefore reduces to owner-only. An ADMIN who is neither the organizer nor an attendee hits the FORBIDDEN throw at lines 54-56. The variable name and the use of `isTeamAdmin` both show that admins were meant to pass. Since `isTeamAdmin` already includes owners, the fix is to drop the `isTeamOwner` call. No test covers this branch.

findings.title: Any booking attendee can add guests, and nothing checks booking status or date
findings.description: Any caller whose session email matches an attendee passes the check. The new guests then receive the standard booking email built from `evt`, which includes location and video call data (lines 136-156). The sibling `editLocation` uses `bookingsProcedure` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/util.ts:19-65), which admits only the organizer or a collective-event member. So this endpoint grants attendees a capability the sibling mutation does not. The handler also never checks `booking.status` or the start time. The UI offers the edit menu on past confirmed bookings (apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:553-554), so cancelled or past bookings can still receive invitations. If attendee access is intended, document it. If not, restrict it and add the status check.

findings.title: Guest list is unbounded and not deduplicated on the server
findings.description: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and no uniqueness check. The uniqueness refine exists only in the dialog (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29). A request that repeats an address passes validation, `uniqueGuests` (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) keeps the duplicates, and `createMany` inserts duplicate attendee rows. Each new guest gets an outbound email, and every call emails all existing attendees (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:539-547). An authenticated caller who passes the permission check can push unlimited mail to arbitrary addresses. Add `.max()` and a server-side uniqueness refine, and move the dialog's schema to module scope so the rules live in one place.

findings.title: Blacklist check is bypassed by letter case
findings.description: The env list is lowercased (line 71), but the input is compared as written (line 77). `Blocked@Example.com` gets through when the list contains `blocked@example.com`. The existing checker lowercases both sides (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts:17-19). Normalize `guest` before both the blacklist check and the existing-attendee comparison (line 76).

findings.title: Guest-added emails are sent from the raw input list, not the filtered one
findings.description: The handler passes `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` treats every address in `newGuests` as new and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541). Everyone else gets `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. So an address that is already an attendee, and that the caller resubmits, receives the "you're scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" one. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Event-type email settings are ignored for guest emails
findings.description: `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no event-type metadata and never checks `disableStandardEmails`. Every other send function in this file does (for example `sendLocationChangeEmails`, lines 495-524). The handler does not pass `booking.eventType.metadata`, even though `eventType` is already loaded (addGuests.handler.ts:32). Hosts who turned off standard emails will still receive guest-added mail. Add the parameter and gate the organizer and attendee sends the way the sibling functions do.

findings.title: Team-member notifications never fire from this handler
findings.description: `sendAddGuestsEmails` notifies team members only when `calendarEvent.team?.members` is set (email-manager.ts:531). The `evt` literal in the handler never sets `team`. `formatCalEvent` (packages/lib/formatCalendarEvent.ts:19-27) only clones the event and rewrites emails, so it does not populate `team`. For collective and round-robin bookings, the non-organizer hosts never get the email. Populate `team` with its members on `evt`, or load them in the handler.

findings.title: Calendar update results are discarded, so failures are reported as success
findings.description: `updateCalendarAttendees` returns `Promise<void>` (packages/core/EventManager.ts:596-602). Per-calendar results from `updateAllCalendarEvents` are dropped, even though that function catches its own errors and returns `success: false` entries (EventManager.ts:921-933). The handler then writes the attendees, sends emails, and returns "Guests added" even if no calendar invite was updated. `editLocation.handler.ts:107-109` checks these results for the same call. Either surface the failure or document the call as best-effort. Also, for non-organizer callers, references without a `credentialId` are matched only against the caller's credentials (EventManager.ts:872-874), so those updates can skip silently.

findings.title: Permission error shows a raw key, and the toast can read "undefined: …"
findings.description: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. When `err.data` is absent (a network failure or a non-tRPC error), the toast reads "undefined: …". The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback on line 44 can never run, because the template string is never empty. The FORBIDDEN path throws `you_do_not_have_permission` (addGuests.handler.ts:55), and that key is missing from apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json, so users see the raw key. Use `err.message` with a real fallback, and add the English string.

findings.title: Dialog state survives closing and successful submits
findings.description: The dialog stays mounted for every row because BookingListItem renders it unconditionally (apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:357-361). `onSuccess` resets the emails but not `isInvalidEmail`. After a validation error followed by a successful submit, the reopened dialog shows "Emails must be unique and valid" over an empty field. Closing via overlay, Escape, or the X calls `setIsOpenDialog` directly (line 61), which skips the reset that Cancel performs (lines 89-93), so typed addresses carry into the next open. Route every close path through one reset function.

findings.title: A second MultiEmail implementation was added instead of replacing the first
findings.description: packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:231-234 already has an inline `multiemail` factory with the same markup, class names, and "Remove email" tooltip, marked `//TODO: Make it a ui component`. This diff creates that component but leaves the form builder on its own copy, so the two will drift. Point the form builder at the new component. The form-builder copy also mutates the `value` array in place, which the new version avoids.

findings.title: No tests cover the new handler, email routing, or dialog
findings.description: The diff contains no test file, and the bookings router folder has no `*.test.ts` files. Nothing covers the authorization branches (the team-admin bug above would have been caught), guest filtering and the blacklist, the recipient routing in `sendAddGuestsEmails`, or the dialog states. Add a handler test with mocked Prisma and EventManager, plus a unit test for `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

findings.title: Email failure is caught without the error object
findings.description: The `catch (err)` discards `err` and logs a fixed string with `console.log`. Swallowing the failure is reasonable here, since the DB writes have already committed. `sendEmail` also logs its own failures, so the loss is partial. Still, `@calcom/lib/logger` is already imported by the sibling `editLocation.handler.ts:5`, and logging `err` with `bookingId` would make this traceable.

findings.title: Unused `credentials: true` include loads credential key material on every call
findings.description: `booking.user.credentials` is never read. Credentials come from `getUsersCredentials` at line 158. The include was copied from `bookingsProcedure` (util.ts:53-57). Drop it.

findings.title: OrganizerAddGuestsEmail uses a different sender name than its sibling
findings.description: `from` uses `APP_NAME`. `OrganizerScheduledEmail` uses `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` (packages/emails/templates/organizer-scheduled-email.ts:47). Pick one, or confirm the difference is intended.

findings.title: The same `add_members` test id is on two elements
findings.description: `TableActions` renders `data-testid={action.id}` (packages/ui/components/table/TableActions.tsx:61, 85), and the menu item uses `id: "add_members"` (BookingListItem.tsx:194). The dialog's submit button uses the same test id, so selectors for either will be ambiguous. Give the submit button its own id.

findings.title: MultiEmail has a hardcoded English label, an unlabeled remove control, and a self-package import
findings.description: The "Remove email" tooltip is a literal string while the rest of the component uses `t()`. The remove button is icon-only with no accessible name, and `label htmlFor="emails"` points at no element. This file is also the only one in packages/ui/form that imports from `"@calcom/ui"` (line 2). That import loops back through the package barrel (packages/ui/index.tsx:153). Use a relative import, a translation key, and an `aria-label`.

findings.title: Router registration, schema, and email wiring are consistent
findings.description: The `addGuests` procedure follows the cache-and-import pattern used by its neighbors. `renderEmail` resolves the new template names through the index, which is where the new exports were added (packages/emails/src/renderEmail.ts:1-7 and packages/emails/src/templates/index.ts). The `title` override is safe: `BaseScheduledEmail` translates `props.title` itself (packages/emails/src/templates/BaseScheduledEmail.tsx:56-62). The keys `additional_guests`, `add_emails`, `new_guests_added`, `guests_added`, `unable_to_add_guests`, `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, and `booking_not_found` all exist in the English locale. The one missing key is `you_do_not_have_permission`, noted above.
